title: Observation of near-infrared fluorescence from within biological specimens using X-ray light-sheet microscopy for deep-tissue imaging

title: Cuproptosis in iron overload hepatocytes
task: Elucidating copper-mediated toxicity mechanism in iron-overloaded hepatocytes
key_results: Copper induces cuproptotic cell death in iron-overloaded hepatocytes via proteotoxic stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, independent of ROS/Fenton chemistry; copper chelation rescued cells
comments: This work elegantly explains phenotypic heterogeneity in hemochromatosis and identifies copper as a critical disease modifier, though the mechanistic link between iron-sulfur cluster damage and proteotoxicity could be explored further.

model_io.model: Hfe knockout mice and Huh7 hepatocytes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Iron overload alone causes overt hepatocyte toxicity
hypotheses.result: Refuted: profound iron loading without copper does not cause toxicity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Copper toxicity is ROS-mediated via Fenton chemistry
hypotheses.result: Refuted: cuproptosis mechanism is independent of ROS damage

hypotheses.hypothesis: Copper chelation can rescue copper-induced toxicity
hypotheses.result: Supported: high-affinity copper chelation rescued cells
